h: From Shad Thames to Holland Park
p: The Design Museum has a bit of a story itself. It was founded by Sir Terence Conran, the man behind Habitat, and first opened in 1989 in a converted warehouse at Shad Thames, near Tower Bridge. In 2016 it moved here to Kensington, into the reworked Commonwealth Institute building with that showstopping roof. The move gave it far more space and turned it into one of the go-to spots in west London for anyone who loves clever ideas.

If you're keeping an eye on the pennies, the permanent collection display, Designer Maker User, is the place to start. It looks at everyday design from three points of view: the person who designs it, the one who makes it and the one who uses it. Expect iconic objects you'll recognise straight away, which makes it a great one for teenagers who might roll their eyes at a more traditional museum.
Allow two to three hours if you're doing an exhibition plus the free displays, and leave time for the shop, which is packed with gadgets, books and gifts you'll want to buy for yourself.

The best bit about the location is what's next door. Holland Park wraps right around the museum, with woodland walks, peacocks and the lovely Kyoto Garden, a peaceful Japanese garden with a waterfall and koi. It's perfect for a picnic or a breather after the galleries. Kensington High Street itself has plenty of shops and places to eat, and High Street Kensington tube station is an easy walk away.
